paper_title: Algorithmic Optimization of the Gaussian Sampler in the FN-DSA Post-Quantum Signature Scheme
statement: Critically, we caution that these routines are not guaranteed to be constant-time. Disassembly of __aeabi_dmul in our toolchain (arm-linux-gnueabi, libgcc) reveals multiple data-dependent conditional branches (beq, bgt) associated with special-case handling (zero operands, exponent normalization, denormalized numbers). Consequently, the constanttime guarantee established in this work applies strictly to the core fixed-point Horner evaluation, not to the end-to-end opt_expm function as currently implemented. A fully constant-time pipeline would require accepting the input x already in fixed-point representation, thereby eliminating all floating-point operations and their associated softfloat calls. This modification requires changing the calling convention of fpr_expm_p63 throughout the FALCON codebase and is identified as essential future work. We emphasize this limitation explicitly: the present contribution demonstrates a constant-time polynomial evaluation core, while achieving a fully isochronous fpr_expm_p63 remains open.
context: 7.2 Residual Soft-Float Calls and Constant-Time Scope Disassembly analysis (Section 6.4) confirms that the core Horner evaluation loop of opt_expm contains zero data-dependent branches, zero FPU instructions, and zero soft-float calls. However, the surrounding argument-reduction steps (computing x · INV_SEG_W and x − seg · SEG_W on double inputs) invoke the ARM EABI soft-float routines __aeabi_dmul and __aeabi_dsub. Critically, we caution that these routines are not guaranteed to be constant-time. Disassembly of __aeabi_dmul in our toolchain (arm-linux-gnueabi, libgcc) reveals multiple data-dependent conditional branches (beq, bgt) associated with special-case handling (zero operands, exponent normalization, denormalized numbers). Consequently, the constanttime guarantee established in this work applies strictly to the core fixed-point Horner evaluation, not to the end-to-end opt_expm function as currently implemented. A fully constant-time pipeline would require accepting the input x already in fixed-point representation, thereby eliminating all floating-point operations and their associated softfloat calls. This modification requires changing the calling convention of fpr_expm_p63 throughout the FALCON codebase and is identified as essential future work. We emphasize this limitation explicitly: the present contribution demonstrates a constant-time polynomial evaluation core, while achieving a fully isochronous fpr_expm_p63 remains open. 7.3 Precision versus Memory Trade-off The ARM configuration (k = 16, d = 3, 256 B) achieves ≈ 2−28 precision, substantially lower than both the x86-64 configuration (≈ 2−52 ) and the theoretical 2−63 target implied by FALCON’s 63-bit output format. As established in Section 5, this precision reduction does not weaken FALCON’s cryptographic security, which is independent of the Gaussian sampler’s numerical precision beyond a very large statistical threshold (≈ 228 signatures under one key). We nonetheless note that this trade-off was a deliberate design choice favoring minimal memory footprint over maximal precision; Table 9 demonstrates that higher-precision configurations (e.g., k = 64, 3584 B) remain available should a target platform’s memory budget permit. 7.4 Comparison Scope Our x86-64 results (Section 5) show performance parity rather than improvement relative to the reference implementation, which itself already employs fixed-point arithmetic with a degree-12 global polynomial (Section 2). This is an expected and informative negative result: on architectures with fast native 64-bit or 128-bit integer multipliers, our segmented approach does not significantly outperform an already carefully optimized FACCT implementation.
